mechanisms.title: High Clearance Vulnerability and Subgroup Failure Under 29 mm Valve STJ and Sinus Limits
mechanisms.explanation: Adding the 29 mm valve size (covering annulusMm 27 mm to 29.5 mm) converts 57 formerly no-fit hearts into assigned hearts, but 19 of those 57 hearts become newly at-risk under the 29 mm valve's stricter clearance limits (31 mm minimum sinotubularJunctionMm for 'stj-excess' and 34 mm minimum sinusMm for 'sinus-clearance'), yielding only 66.6666666666667% fit (38 of 57) in that subgroup (disproving the claim fitPct >= 69.25). Across the full 400-heart development cohort, total at-risk hearts increase to 87 (70 failing 'stj-excess' and 47 failing 'sinus-clearance'), and many newly fitted 29 mm hearts sit just above the 31 mm STJ threshold (e.g., heart-060 has sinotubularJunctionMm 31.0223611138226 mm and heart-498 has sinotubularJunctionMm 31.0132319990659 mm, while newly at-risk heart-019 has sinotubularJunctionMm 29.9892814019414 mm vs limit 31, margin -1.01071859805864, and sinusMm 32.7155227494946 mm vs limit 34, margin -1.28447725050541). Profiling the 19 newly at-risk 29 mm hearts shows that while their annulusMm (groupMean 27.6457836404053 mm vs restMean 24.4817734343911 mm, effect size 1.27930535103958) and lvotMm (groupMean 28.8855979065385 mm vs restMean 23.9721468804493 mm, effect size 1.4615777316538) are much larger than the rest of the cohort, their sinotubularJunctionMm (groupMean 29.9465404515047 mm vs restMean 29.5480969253527 mm, effect size 0.137595059562471) fails to scale proportionally. Consequently, stress tests easily break the proposal's claim of fitPct >= 69.25%: a +1 mm assumption shift drops fitPct from 69.25% (277 fit) to 53.5% (214 fit, 150 at risk, 63 changed from fit to risk); a -1 mm measurement shift in sinotubularJunctionMm drops fitPct to 58% (232 fit, 132 at risk, 45 changed from fit to risk); and a -1 mm measurement shift in sinusMm drops fitPct to 60.5% (242 fit, 122 at risk, 35 changed from fit to risk).

mechanisms.title: Sensitivity to Annulus Measurement Shifts and Upper 29.5 mm Boundary Overflow
mechanisms.explanation: Under a +1 mm measurement shift in annulusMm, the proposed design's fitPct collapses from 69.25% (277 fit, 87 risk, 36 no-fit) to 52.75% (211 fit, 155 risk, 34 no-fit), with 102 hearts changing status. This occurs via two mechanisms: first, borderline fit hearts across sizes 23, 25, and 27 are upsized into the next larger valve size where they fail the stricter 'stj-excess' or 'sinus-clearance' thresholds; second, 18 hearts in the upper portion of the 29 mm size range (15 fit hearts and 3 at-risk hearts, such as heart-498 with annulusMm 29.1833633257593 mm) are pushed above the 29.5 mm maximum annulus limit into 'no-fit'. Additionally, a what_if test narrowing the 29 mm size's maxAnnulusMm from 29.5 mm to 29 mm (matching the 2 mm width of sizes 23, 25, and 27) causes 11 of the newly fitted hearts (heart-161, heart-173, heart-179, heart-223, heart-268, heart-373, heart-446, heart-481, heart-489, heart-498) and 1 at-risk heart (heart-375) to revert to 'no-fit', showing that the 69.25% fit claim relies heavily on the extra 0.5 mm upper annulus extension (29 to 29.5 mm).

Profiling the 93 no-fit hearts against the rest of the cohort shows higher mean lvotMm (26.2397743438473 vs 23.5893006765396, effect size 0.78842208254492) and annulusMm (26.1196504829399 vs 24.1814269470922, effect size 0.783682598813269) due to the larger share of oversized annuli.

52 hearts are placed at risk by rule 'stj-excess' because their sinotubularJunctionMm is smaller than the required minimum STJ limit for their assigned valve size (such as a 27 mm limit for size 25 and a 29 mm limit for size 27). Profiling these 52 hearts shows they have markedly narrower sinotubular junctions than the rest of the cohort (groupMean 26.5045097370466 mm vs restMean 30.0246399161251 mm, difference -3.52013017907853 mm, effect size -1.2156114728117), narrower sinusMm (groupMean 30.5892482692222 mm vs restMean 33.1623513220977 mm, effect size -0.772725978362664), and higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (groupMean 1.02645440665182 vs restMean 0.953344983673109, effect size 0.682085964814614) while having similar annulusMm (groupMean 24.2162817933461 mm vs restMean 24.6941922828066 mm, effect size -0.193233715024884). Inspected examples include heart-014 (assigned size 27, sinotubularJunctionMm 26.8311463740637 vs limit 29, margin -2.16885362593629), heart-001 (assigned size 27, sinotubularJunctionMm 28.5705544474013 vs limit 29, margin -0.42944555259869), and heart-086 (assigned size 25, sinotubularJunctionMm 26.48261056391 vs limit 27, margin -0.517389436090028).

input.rationale: Adding a 29 mm valve size covering annulus diameters from 27 mm to 29.5 mm directly addresses the oversized annulus segment of the annulus-coverage failure mechanism above the 27 mm maximum limit. This single change reduces no-fit hearts from 93 to 36 and increases fit on the 400 development hearts from 59.75% (239 hearts) to 69.25% (277 hearts), a +9.5 percentage point improvement.
tradeOffs: Assigning previously uncovered hearts with annulus diameters between 27 mm and 29.5 mm to the new 29 mm size transitions some formerly no-fit hearts (such as heart-019) to at-risk status, increasing total at-risk hearts from 68 to 87.

36 hearts remain with no-fit status (including those below the 21 mm minimum limit and above the 29.5 mm maximum limit), and existing stj-excess and sinus-clearance risks in the 23, 25, and 27 mm sizes are not modified by this change.
